domain: Lunar New Year dinner for family
base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a Lunar New Year family dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary needs, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, my family is getting together for Lunar New Year dinner this year and I'm in charge of the menu. Can you help me plan it?

flow_info.value: Five of us confirmed so far: me, my mom, my dad, my older sister Mei, and my brother-in-law Kevin
Dad had a bad gout flare-up last month, doctor put him on medication and told him to watch what he eats
Mei just told us she's 4 months pregnant, the whole family is thrilled
Kevin ate satay skewers at a hawker stall once and his throat swelled up so bad they had to use an EpiPen
Hoping to keep it around 300 total for ingredients since we're cooking at home
My nephew Ethan, Mei's 4-year-old, is coming too — almost forgot about the little guy
Dad just told me his doctor cleared him last week — gout is under control, medication is done, he can eat normally again
Uncle Hong just called and said he's driving down to join us after all, so that's one more

Uncle Hong has been living in Chiang Mai for the past ten years, became really devout — he ordained as a monk for a while and even now he still keeps the precepts strictly, no alcohol, no killing, the whole thing
Dishes to check: whole steamed fish, kung pao chicken, longevity noodles with peanut sauce, raw salmon yusheng, braised pork belly, stir-fried vegetables with oyster sauce

constraints.value: Must avoid high-purine foods: organ meats, shellfish, red meat in excess, alcohol
constraints.surface_form: Dad had a bad gout flare-up last month, doctor put him on medication and told him to watch what he eats
inference_chain: High uric acid → must avoid high-purine foods
High-purine foods → organ meats, shellfish, excessive red meat, alcohol

constraints.value: Must avoid raw or undercooked fish/meat, high-mercury fish, alcohol
constraints.surface_form: Mei just told us she's 4 months pregnant, the whole family is thrilled
inference_chain: 4 months pregnant → pregnancy dietary restrictions apply
Pregnancy → no raw fish/meat, no alcohol, avoid high-mercury fish

constraints.surface_form: Kevin ate satay skewers at a hawker stall once and his throat swelled up so bad they had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Satay skewers → peanut sauce is the signature component
Throat swelling + EpiPen → anaphylactic allergic reaction
Allergic reaction to satay → peanut allergy

constraints.surface_form: Oh and Ethan can't have eggs — Mei found out the hard way when he broke out in hives after eating a custard bun
inference_chain: Hives after custard bun → allergic reaction
Allergic reaction to custard bun → egg allergy

constraints.value: Strict Buddhist vegetarian — no meat, no fish, no alcohol, no killing of animals
constraints.surface_form: Uncle Hong has been living in Chiang Mai for the past ten years, became really devout — he ordained as a monk for a while and even now he still keeps the precepts strictly, no alcohol, no killing, the whole thing
inference_chain: Ordained as Buddhist monk + still keeps precepts strictly → devout Buddhist
Devout Buddhist keeping precepts → vegetarian, no alcohol, no killing

hidden_state.value: You are planning a Lunar New Year family dinner. You will introduce family members and their backgrounds across several turns. The guest list and constraints will change — your dad's gout clears up, your nephew joins, and your Uncle Hong joins late with strict dietary needs. At the end, you will present a list of dishes and ask if there are any issues. You must present the exact dish list and ask naturally. You never hint at what the problems might be.

You are a warm, easygoing family member coordinating a holiday dinner. You relay updates about relatives in third person (e.g. 'Dad just told me...', 'Uncle Hong called and said...'). You never express frustration or impatience — changing plans are just how family gatherings work. You are matter-of-fact and cheerful.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for family updates

ground_truth.answer: Four dishes have clear problems. Whole steamed fish: Uncle Hong is a strict Buddhist vegetarian, cannot eat fish. Kung pao chicken: Uncle Hong cannot eat chicken (vegetarian), and kung pao chicken traditionally contains peanuts which Kevin is severely allergic to. Longevity noodles with peanut sauce: Kevin has a severe peanut allergy (anaphylactic reaction to satay), peanut sauce is dangerous. Raw salmon yusheng: Mei is 4 months pregnant, cannot eat raw fish. Braised pork belly: Uncle Hong cannot eat pork (vegetarian). Stir-fried vegetables with oyster sauce is fine for everyone — it is a vegetable dish and oyster sauce is not a problem for anyone currently attending. Dad's gout restriction no longer applies since his doctor cleared him.
required_elements: Whole steamed fish is problematic: Uncle Hong is a strict Buddhist vegetarian and cannot eat fish
Kung pao chicken is problematic: Uncle Hong cannot eat chicken (vegetarian), AND kung pao chicken contains peanuts which Kevin is severely allergic to
Longevity noodles with peanut sauce is problematic: Kevin has a severe peanut allergy — his throat swelled up from satay skewers and required an EpiPen
Raw salmon yusheng is problematic: Mei is 4 months pregnant and cannot eat raw fish
Braised pork belly is problematic: Uncle Hong is a strict Buddhist vegetarian and cannot eat pork
Agent confirms dad has no dietary restrictions anymore since his doctor cleared him last week
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish as problematic for dad's gout (his doctor cleared him, restriction removed)
Saying Kevin has a general nut allergy or seafood allergy (he specifically has a peanut allergy inferred from satay reaction)

Flagging stir-fried vegetables with oyster sauce as problematic for Uncle Hong (oyster sauce is a condiment, not meat — standard Buddhist vegetarian practice varies but this is not a clear violation in common knowledge)

Saying Ethan cannot eat the longevity noodles due to egg allergy without verifying whether these specific noodles contain egg (noodles may or may not contain egg depending on recipe — agent should note the possibility, not assert it as certain)
Flagging dishes as too rich or heavy for dad (his restriction is fully removed)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 turns. The agent must track: (1) Dad's gout → high-purine diet restriction (inferential), which is then REMOVED when his doctor clears him — agent must not ghost this constraint onto the probe. (2) Mei's pregnancy → no raw fish/meat (inferential). (3) Kevin's satay reaction → peanut allergy (3-step inferential chain: satay → peanut sauce → peanut allergy). (4) Ethan joins with egg allergy (inferential from custard bun hives). (5) Uncle Hong joins LATE (turn 5 of 8) as a high-constraint entity: ordained Buddhist monk who keeps precepts → strict vegetarian, no alcohol, no killing. Uncle Hong is the primary difficulty driver — he joins late and his constraint affects 4 of 6 dishes. The over-generalization trap is on Kevin: peanut allergy ≠ all nut allergy. The removed-constraint trap is dad's gout. The stir-fried vegetables with oyster sauce is the 'looks bad but isn't' trap — oyster sauce is a common condiment and not a meat product in standard understanding.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
